_comment: Export admissions for packages/principles-core. Schema and rules: scripts/check-core-export-surface.mjs. Every record needs expiresAt; consumers are parsed and must import AND use the symbol.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Console and CLI packages must resolve the two workspace database paths; without a public subpath every consumer keeps its own '.pd' / '.state' path.join literal, which is exactly the drift this batch removes.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-exporting the resolvers from the wide ./runtime barrel, rejected because that entry already carries 2,032 symbols and this batch must not widen it.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console runs in a separate package that cannot import core-internal relative modules; it needs the single workspace-state path authority at runtime.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Copying the '.pd/state.db' literal in each console model, rejected because that keeps 20+ independent path authorities.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console opens trajectory.db directly for read-only counts and pain lookups; it cannot reach the core-internal storage-paths module by relative import.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Importing it from ./trajectory-store, rejected because that entry is the trajectory API surface, not the workspace path contract.

admissions.whyNotInternal: host-runtime owns the live decision gate in a separate package and cannot use a core-internal relative import; this subpath is the single input-assembly contract shared with Golden Trace replay, so the two paths cannot derive workspace.isRiskPath differently.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Re-exporting through the wide ./runtime barrel was rejected: it widens an already large public surface and hides which contract the host actually needs.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Provider keys are resolved in five separate processes (console, host-runtime classifier/selection, pd-cli probe and rule-host). They live in different packages and cannot import a core-internal module; without one shared resolver each process keeps its own env lookup and the local credentials file silently stops working for the agents the Owner configured.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Adding apiKey values to .pd/config.yaml was rejected: ADR-0016 still forbids secret fields in config.yaml, and the validator keeps rejecting them. Duplicating the file reader per process was rejected because it recreates the precedence rule (env first) and the YAML schema in every consumer.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console runs in a separate package and cannot import the core-internal pi-ai catalog bridge. It needs the same read-only projection the runtime already trusts, otherwise the picker would ship a second, hand-maintained provider/model list.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Importing @earendil-works/pi-ai directly in pd-console was rejected: the catalog entry shapes would then be interpreted twice (adapter and console), and the console would drift from the runtime's provider validation.

admissions.whyNotInternal: The console route must run the exact same provider/model resolution and transport classification the runtime uses; a console-local HTTP probe would validate a different code path than the one that actually runs agents.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Calling `pd runtime probe` as a subprocess was rejected: it adds a process boundary, a second error serialization format, and cannot classify model-list vs chat stages without parsing CLI text.

admissions.whyNotInternal: Stage-2 classification runs in two other packages (the shared host-runtime classifier factory and the OpenClaw plugin host that owns the trajectory). Both must construct and pass the same fact shape into the core-owned prompt builder; a relative core-internal import is not possible across packages, and duplicating the shape would create a second contract for the same evidence.
admissions.alternativeConsidered: Inlining a structural type in each consumer was rejected: the prompt builder and the gate would then accept shapes no shared type constrains, which is exactly how the R3 'no behavioral fact' misclassification reached admission.
